title: Geometries for the group PSL(3,4)
edition: Halle Reports on Algebra and Geometry99-30; institutional complete22-page PostScript preprint, TeX timestamp1999-12-02, locally converted PDF. Not collated with25-page EJC24(2003),267–291 journal version.

items.claim: Classify up to geometry isomorphism all firm, residually connected PSL(3,4)-flag-transitive RWPRI IP2 geometries; local2T is an output, not an assumed filter. Ranks2,3,4,5,>=6 give7,7,11,4,0.
Distinct parabolics, left cosets, incidence by nonempty intersection; flags/chambers, residues, firmness, kernels, faithful action, RWPRI/IP2/local2T, type-preserving Aut versus Cor.
A pregeometry is a residually connected geometry iff its displayed subgroup lattice is strongly Boolean.
items.role: quoted Tits reference45; literal hypotheses retained as reading obligation

items.claim: For an arbitrary chosen alpha(J) in each nonempty J, full geometry/flag transitivity iff intersection of Gj*Galpha equals (intersection Gj)*Galpha for all |J|>=3.
Unique plane of order4; three56-hyperoval and three120-Baer-subplane orbits; butterfly uniqueness from either stated subplane pair or subplane+central pair.
Ordered butterflies distinguish + and − poles; every butterfly has two choices, transitive under PSL(3,4).
An ordered butterfly has stabilizer C2×D8, hence order16;1260 ordered butterflies per designated orbit.
Four complement quadrangles determine two + and two − hyperovals with the specified central-line points.
Doubling for finite rank>=3 residually connected geometries satisfying exact I12 shadow condition and displayed diagram; residual connectivity and stated odd-gonality relation preserved.
items.role: quoted reference40; weaker hypothesis than Pasini full IP
